​⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An Unforgettable Morning at Sweet Maple
​If you are looking for the absolute gold standard of breakfast, Sweet Maple is in a league of its own. From the moment you walk through the doors, the timeless, welcoming ambiance sets the perfect mood—warm, vibrant, and classic without trying too hard.
​The menu is packed with hits, but a few standouts make this place an absolute must-visit:
​The Blackstone Benedict: Perfectly poached eggs and rich, velvety hollandaise layered over savory bacon and sliced tomatoes. Every single bite is pure perfection.
​The French Toast: Decadent, golden, and melt-in-your-mouth tender. It hits the exact right balance of sweet and indulgent without feeling overly heavy.
​The beverage game here is just as strong:
​Bloody Marys: Bold, perfectly spiced, and served with just the right kick to kick off the morning.
​Cappuccinos: Expertly crafted with rich espresso and silky, smooth foam—a coffee lover’s dream.
​Beyond the incredible food and drink, the service was top-tier. The staff was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming from start to finish, ensuring everything arrived fresh and fast despite a busy dining room.
​Sweet Maple effortlessly balances incredible food with a warm, timeless atmosphere. 5 out of 5 stars—we will be back again and again!

Such a great find just off Third Street Promenade!

My family and I were walking around Third Street Promenade and were in the mood for really good Italian food. We heard about UOVO, walked one block over to Second Street, and I’m so glad we did.

One of the things that makes it so special is that all of the pasta is handmade in Italy using Italian ingredients and flown overnight to the restaurant every day.

We ordered the yellowtail carpaccio, lasagna, carbonara, and tonnarelli with pomodoro sauce. Everything was delicious, and everyone loved it, including the kids. We were enjoying the food so much that I forgot to take pictures of the pasta, but I did manage to snap one of the yellowtail!

The staff was friendly and attentive. UOVO is also a no-tipping restaurant. A 16% service charge is automatically added to the bill and they do not accept additional tips. Since we normally tip 20%, that was perfectly fine with us.

Really delicious food and such a fun family dinner.

Such an awesome lunch spot overall, and I’ll definitely be back for more.

text.text:
Capo – Santa Monica, CA
Rating: ★★★☆☆
Having come up in the industry working for Joseph Pignato at The Rivermere in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, I know exactly what technical precision looks like. When you’ve operated at that level—or dined at institutions like The Blue Strawberry—you develop a palate that doesn't settle for "almost." My standard for pasta is set by the likes of Lievito Bistro in Nicaragua, run by my wife’s brother-in-law who learned his passion for cooking in Italy. When you've experienced his daily handmade pasta—crafted with the authentic passion and soul of a chef straight from Italy—you know exactly when a kitchen is missing that heart. At a $687 price point, Capo's execution needs to be surgical, and tonight, it felt mechanical.
Technical Hits and Misses
* The Scallop Black Truffle ($96): This was the major disappointment of the evening. The sear was pushed too far, leaving a carbonized, burnt flavor that masked the delicate scallop and fought against the truffle. For nearly $100, that plate should be flawless; tonight, it was a technical failure.
* Lobster Pasta ($60): The lobster itself was the highlight—delicious and perfectly cooked. However, the kitchen was heavy-handed with the salt, nearly overshadowing the natural sweetness of the meat.
* The Pomodoro ($28): When you’re used to the fresh, vibrant pasta at Lievito Bistro, you notice the details.
Service and Logistics
Service from Roger was great, along with his hospitality.He earned the 20 gratuity. But adding it as a line item feels like a disconnect from a "guest-first" philosophy.
The Bottom Line
There is talent here, but the lack of consistency is glaring.
I have to say that my old fashioned was delicious and perfect and my wife's lemon drop was spot on. At $100+ per person, I expect much more  from the food consistency.  My wife is a USC graduate with a D.D.S. and also has high expectations... and noted the burt taste and smell of the scallops and the salty Lobster. Having grown up in New England and having a fisherman  and lobsterman deliver fresh live fish off the boat at the restraunt dock every morning I also know what to expect with such a dish.... So.... stick to the fresh daily made pasta dishes, and know that kitchen consistency may not meet the reputation or price.... yet expect an amazing dining experience in a staple of Santa Monica.

This restaurant made our celebration of my daughter’s 19th birthday even more memorable. We highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys delicious food, warm service, and spectacular ocean views—especially after sunset.

text.text:
Warning: do not come to this place.

First of all, we had a reservation for 8:00 PM. As soon as we arrived and walked through the door, the reception area was completely packed with people. There was barely any room to stand. We were told that, regardless of having a reservation, we would need to wait around 20–30 minutes because of how crowded it was. In the end, we were seated at a table all the way at the back at 8:59 PM — almost one full hour after our reservation time.

At least the staff working at the small bar upstairs, where guests are asked to wait, were friendly. There was only one girl working alone behind a bar full of people. This is not really the employees' fault, but rather a consequence of how the restaurant is managed. It was obvious that the staff were overwhelmed and unable to keep up with demand. There are around 15 teppanyaki stations and only 4 chefs. Since each station serves two tables, that's effectively 30 tables, with each chef handling two stations at the same time.

Once seated, our order was not taken until 9:20 PM. Again, this was not the fault of the staff, who were clearly overworked and understaffed. We then had to wait another 20 minutes for the first appetizers, which were just a simple soup and salad that should not take long to prepare. In fact, I did not eat any cooked food until 10:15 PM.

One positive aspect is that the chefs are not restricted to a fixed, scripted performance. They have quite a lot of personality and interact with guests, make jokes, and create their own atmosphere, which was enjoyable.

The restaurant itself was extremely dirty. The floors were covered with paper scraps and other trash, there were pieces of food everywhere, the railings felt sticky, and even the restroom was somewhat dirty.

In the end, we were able to speak with the manager about the situation. He acknowledged the issues and gave us a discount on the bill, which allowed us to leave the tip that the waitstaff genuinely deserved. Throughout the evening, the servers remained professional, friendly, and did the best they could under very difficult circumstances.

Overall, the experience was a little disappointing. The main issue is not the staff, but poor management, insufficient capacity, and a lack of personnel for the number of customers they are trying to serve.

We went here on a fall evening for drinks and appetizers to celebrate a couple birthdays since there is nothing nicer than seeing the gorgeous sunset while drinking a cocktail at the beach. Shutters Hotel is right on the beach in Santa Monica and the Coast Cafe is one of their oceanfront cafes. The unobstructed view of the water is worth the high prices of the food and drink for a special occasion. We happen to be there on a Friday Night which is “pizza night” and we all shared a Margarita Pizza that had nice thin crust and was cooked in their wood-fired pizza oven. The menu had several VEGAN options, including a vegan dessert, which I really appreciated and I would most certainly come back again to try. Cocktails in fall 2025 were $22 each which is about average for a beachfront restaurant in a hotel. Our server, Jesse, was great, very friendly and checking on us constantly. We never felt rushed even though we were there for just drinks and appetizers during weekend dinner hour. There was a musician on the beach path in front of our table (see photo) playing soft tunes which added to the chill vibe and beach atmosphere of our experience. He overhead that we had some birthdays in our group (yes he was that close) and he beautifully sang Happy Birthday to each person individually which we really enjoyed. I don’t believe he is employed by the hotel and yes we gave him a well-deserved tip.  All in all and great experience.

If you’re looking for great Mexican food, excellent drinks, and a fun atmosphere in Venice Beach, this place is definitely worth visiting!

This was the worst fish and chips I’ve ever had. The draft beer was disappointing too. The glass was cold, but the beer itself wasn’t.

The fish and chips tasted like they were fried in old oil. The fish had a strong ocean-water taste, seemed like a very cheap type of fish, and was watery inside, almost as if it wasn’t cooked all the way through.

The only positive was the large screen for watching the game. When we arrived, the hostess asked us to share a booth with another couple because there were only two of us. We agreed, but no one ever joined us. Then, unbelievably, she brought a random man over and seated him in our booth. That was very awkward and uncomfortable. She kept telling us to stay where we were instead of letting us have the booth to ourselves during the game.

The air conditioning also wasn’t working. It was hot inside with almost no fresh air, making the experience very uncomfortable.

Overall, this is not a sports bar I would recommend. We usually go to Barney’s Beanery on 3rd Street, where the food, drinks, service, and atmosphere are much better.

We were wandering along the coastline in Santa Monica and looked for an eatery nearby. Kings Head was open, and we hadn’t had fish & chips in a while, so walked over. Very pleasant place - pub atmosphere inside and some sidewalk patio seating. We were promptly seated, and our server was attentive. We ordered the side salad and two piece fish & chips to share.

If you’re not a big eater, it would be easy to share the two piece. The pieces are (seriously) the size of small burritos, and you get a pile of fries. The salad was mid-sized and nice. The photo posted gives you a pretty good idea of portion sizes.

I would definitely recommend this place - and will keep it in mind when we’re in the area!
